A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework and retain corresponding application sections. All pages, figures, equations and appendices support comparison. Earlier Appendices A.4–A.7 correspond to later B.1–B.4; Appendix C is new.

before.justification: v1 reports original computed geodesics, decoded interpolation and extrapolation examples, and torus projection-error experiments in Section 5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds letter-image experiments and numerical comparisons with competing geodesic methods in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The projection loss and variational geodesic algorithms are retained. However, Section 5.2 changes the specified decoder output used in geometric computations from a sampled decoding to the decoder distribution's mean, a limited revision to the reported inference procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds rotated-and-scaled letter-A images, a synthetic 3D point-cloud/VAE example, and noisy half-circle data (Figures 2, 16 and 17). The torus, SCAPE, CMU motion-capture, rotating-cow and Pose-NDF coverage is retained, so the expansion principally concerns additional synthetic scenarios.

E2.justification: Appendix C newly evaluates Stochman's parametric geodesic and exponential solvers, the RBF-based method of Arvanitidis et al. (2018), sigmoid uncertainty regularization from Arvanitidis et al. (2022), and LAND. LAND is also added to the retained cow-image comparison. These substantially extend v1's linear-interpolation and internal metric comparisons.

E3.justification: New protocols include 50-node torus paths versus eight-node splines with 50 metric evaluations and 2000 optimization iterations, plus half-circle tests using 6000 points and K=30. Motion-capture settings now specify decoder means and Leaky ReLU projection activations, differing from v1's sampled outputs and general ELU specification. These revisions do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds examinations of whether exponential shooting reproduces a minimizing torus path, stability with widely separated half-circle endpoints, and off-manifold failures or decoded artifacts in competing methods. The earlier torus noise, sampling-density and network-size sensitivity study remains unchanged as Figure 11.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The added timings and trajectories introduce no new statistical uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds numerical and qualitative comparison results. For example, C.1 reports torus energy/time of 4.7889/1.89 seconds for the proposed approach and 4.7892/2.48 seconds for Stochman under their respective discretizations. C.3–C.4 add runtime, nonconvergence and artifact findings. The motion-extrapolation example is also replaced; these are new or replaced results, not demonstrated v1-to-v2 performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the convergence approximation condition from O(dist^-3) to O(dist^3). It also adds reasoning explaining why exponential-map optimization avoids second-order differentiation of the projection and decoder networks. The central variational definitions and convergence claims otherwise remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about implicit latent manifolds, denoising projections, geodesic interpolation/extrapolation and compatibility with different autoencoders and metrics. The more precise title and expanded introduction clarify this existing scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds substantive interpretations involving variational consistency, negative-curvature instability, off-manifold metric construction and codimension. It discusses projection-training overhead and competing methods' applicability restrictions. Figure 12 additionally interprets similar linear and geodesic shell paths as evidence of local flatness; earlier limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 documents a PyTorch L-BFGS implementation alongside SciPy BFGS, explicitly specifies noisy inputs as y_z=z+epsilon, and adds initialization and penalty guidance. Appendix C supplies comparator discretizations, half-circle network and data parameters, penalty limits, LAND hyperparameters, and training/computation times, substantially expanding technical reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Appendix C substantially expands positioning relative to parametric, graph-based, uncertainty-regularized and density-based approaches. New references include LAND, robust shortest-path methods, Stochman, Fermat distances and diffusion-based geodesics. Existing Arvanitidis references receive detailed methodological comparisons, and the discussion of Shao et al. is revised to emphasize nonzero latent-manifold codimension.

P1.justification: The title is refined, introduction and related-work passages are rewritten, and explanations of differentiation and initialization are expanded. Existing appendix material is regrouped into method and experiment details, followed by the new comparison appendix. Most existing main-text prose and its section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 2 and comparison Figures 15–18, and replaces the motion-extrapolation display while removing its latent-space panel. Figure 18 redisplays existing cow outputs beside new LAND results. Other figures are largely retained with revised numbering, placement or captions, producing a substantial expansion of the visual evidence.

improvement.justification: v1's comparative validation relied chiefly on linear interpolation and internal metric variants. Appendix C substantially addresses this gap through direct comparisons with established alternatives, including energy, runtime, stability and failure evidence. Together with the corrected convergence condition and expanded implementation guidance, this materially improves assessment of the framework's value and applicability. The comparisons remain largely illustrative and do not establish general superiority.
